cards.note: npm package with dsh.bundle.patch; installed through the official path (`dsh plugin --profile web add`) and composed as a dsh.profile.bundles layer in an isolated profile
no legacy dshClient field and no dsh.plugin.json; dsh.client already carries platform web plus the ./client entry
dsh.client is declared with platform web and the ./client export; the live boot manifest composes the row under the package name
every service the browser half touches is declared (sessions, locale, slots); the host half consumes none and uses no ctx.get
no optional host service is probed and ctx.get is never used
no session/event subscription; the generating flag is selected from the sessions list state through the seat's useSessions hook
the target client plane provides ctx.sessions (ISessions) and the useSessions seat is bound to the same list store; Node-half aggregation was the 0810-0812 window recipe only
the plugin never tails task/run output and does not use tasks.read/peek
no host service injection at all, so none of httpServer/webServer, tasks/jobs or onTaskDone/onJobDone appears
no ImageAttachmentRef, read_image output or persisted image metadata
the plugin neither registers, wraps nor parses read_image output
no custom LLM adapter, image interceptor or attachment cache
no APIProxy or ctx.remote call site; the browser half only consumes cordis services
the target is alpha.2 and the plugin produces no persisted SessionEvents
no host-source patch and no internal session-view import; the plugin uses public services only
no launcher/SDK wrapper and no profile-file reader; the official DSH_HOME profile path is used for installation and composition
no headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parser in the plugin
the plugin does not use the tool presentation mode, PTC presets or the dispatch waterfall
no permission/approval/WebFetch policy or audit surface
no custom loopback HTTP/WS/RPC route or custom /api handler; the plugin registers no webserver route
not a model provider plugin; no provider login configuration to integrate
the plugin registers its own copy namespace for existing languages via ctx.locale.register; it ships no custom language pack or i18n patch
no subagent orchestration or provider/model selector surface
informational: the plugin neither configures nor documents the DeepSeek adapter's package-name reporting, and its own code needs no change
no PowerShell/Bash persistence or Windows directory-picker workaround to retire
no session-log upload or watermark handling
the plugin ships no browser acceptance script; the migration's own check followed this recipe against an isolated profile
no structured-question answerer registration
the plugin does not infer an agent preset from a persisted session
no token-delta detection or TPS computation
the bundle layer only inserts the plugin row and restates no telemetry or inventory configuration, so there is no privacy stance to preserve
@earendil-works/pi-ai is not a dependency of this plugin
@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime removed from dsh.client.inject, peers and JSDoc; ClientContext is now cordis Context with sessions/locale/types supplied by their owning packages

the shipped ./client artifact is now the lazy-CJS closure factory registering under package.json#name (previously the source-form ESM file failed the boot with 'loaded without registering'); insert row and graph row both use the same package name
the overlay reads only the running flag; it reads no timeline or user message content
the plugin does not touch the composer DOM
no MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlock rendering
no ctx.connection.api consumption; the plugin reads no history or transcript
no subagent descriptor construction or assertion
no ctx.workspaces or ctx.uiWorkspace usage and no workspace snapshot fields read
the plugin produces no persisted SessionEvents
no ctx.remote unary call or RemoteResult handling
peer cohort recomposed for alpha.2 (removed dsh-client-runtime; added the type owners ui-layout/ui-renderer; all optional) and verified by an isolated-profile install plus cold boot
the plugin carries no Node-version workaround; verification ran on Node 24.21.0, outside the 24.0-24.11.1 failure window
the plugin does not consume the plugin inventory snapshot
no host.describe call and no host home/loopback fact needed
the plugin mounts through the shipped web bundle instead of composing its own profile, and lists none of the affected tool/agent packages as peers
the plugin registers, reads and writes no settings namespace; configuration stays on the documented bundle-row config block, which the pending harness patch forwards to the browser half
